summary: Python SDK + custom transport (chunked) causes idempotency header split and duplicate webhook function-call
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated external webhook/tool/function invocations when using our Python SDK with a custom HTTP transport that emits chunked transfer-encoding. The duplicated executions happen only after a transient connection failure when the SDK's background retry thread re-sends the request.

Impact: NimbleDocs sees duplicate downstream jobs (billing+side-effects) for a subset (~2%) of long-running function calls. This is causing data duplication and customer-visible incorrect state.

Environment: NimbleDocs is on a Dedicated plan in us-east using Python SDK v1.8.2, custom requests.Session adapter that enables HTTP/2 multiplexing and chunked body streaming via iter_bytes. Edge sits behind an internal sidecar that rewrites some headers for routing.

Expected behavior: Retries should be safe and idempotent when an idempotency header is present; duplicate webhook/tool invocations should be prevented by the SDK or upstream dedupe.

Actual behavior: After a mid-request connection reset, SDK retries the request and downstream webhook receives two invocations with different idempotency-header representations. Edge/proxy treats them as separate requests and forwards both to the customer's job queue.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a Python client using Python SDK v1.8.2 and pass a custom requests.Session with an HTTP/2-capable transport and chunked streaming body (yielding small chunks).
2) Call the API with a function/tool that triggers an external webhook callback (long-running: 20-30s). Include X-Idempotency-Key header generated per logical operation.
3) Simulate a transient connection reset from the edge (tcp reset or short-lived proxy restart) during the streaming of the request body.
4) Observe client background retry logic: SDK re-sends the request (re-using session/transport) from a retry worker thread.

5) Inspect downstream webhook logs: two separate requests arrive; idempotency header values differ in byte representation (one split across chunk boundary), and the edge/proxy does not normalize them, so dedupe fails.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Support initial triage: reproduced with NimbleDocs test harness running local edge-proxy (sidecar) and custom chunk sizes. Duplicates observed when header bytes get split across chunk boundary and edge-proxy does not reassemble/normalize header canonicalization.

2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - Eng (Priya) note: SDK retry worker reuses the same transport and replays the request; requests library will stream chunks again. When the header is large or contains characters that result in splitting (some proxies limit header line length), the proxy may apply header folding which changed representation.

2026-03-11 02:10 UTC - Networking: Edge sidecar logs show header folding (RFC 7230 continuation) on h2-to-h1 translation. Downstream webhook endpoint treats the two different representations as distinct idempotency keys (one has an inserted hyphen during reassembly in our test).

Hypothesis: Combination of chunked transfer, custom transport, and edge/proxy header folding leads to byte-level idempotency-key mutation across the retry boundary. Downstream dedupe based on literal header string fails, causing duplicate processing.

Attempted mitigations run: 1) Reproduced with standard requests.Session (no custom transport) - no duplicates. 2) Reproduced with small chunk size and HTTP/2 prior-knowledge - duplicates. 3) Forcing SDK to send idempotency key in body (instead of header) prevents duplication but breaks some customers' orchestration.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Hector Alvarez): Hi NimbleDocs team — thanks for the report and repro steps. We're prioritizing this as P1 due to downstream side-effects. Can you share the exact custom transport code (or a minimized snippet) and an example idempotency key format you generate?

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (NimbleDocs - engineering): Sent snippet (attached in support portal). Idempotency key is a 12-char alphanumeric token (example: XGK-abc123). We confirmed behavior only on a dedicated edge setup that rewrites headers for routing. Using the public hosted API doesn't reproduce.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Support (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally with NimbleDocs snippet. Raising to runtime/edge team for advice on header canonicalization. Adding labels and linking to similar routing tickets.

2026-03-11 08:40 - Edge Team (Marcus Li): Edge performs h2->h1 header serialization and may insert continuation markers when a single header exceeds internal framing thresholds. We're investigating whether we should normalize idempotency header whitespace and punctuation during translation.

2026-03-12 16:22 - Support (Priya Nair): Workaround tested: customer can set SDK flag 'idempotency_in_body=true' to place the token in JSON payload (server-side dedupe also checks payload). This prevents duplicates for their workflow. We documented steps and recommended short-term config change while we build a fix.
resolution: Workaround applied: NimbleDocs toggled idempotency_in_body flag to true (server accepts fallback payload key). Root cause: header byte fragmentation across chunk boundaries combined with edge h2->h1 translation that performs header folding/continuation, leading to mutated idempotency-key values. Fix plan: 1) Short-term: ship SDK update v1.8.3 that ensures idempotency header is sent as a single header frame (avoid chunked header emission) and adds optional header canonicalization helper. 2) Mid-term: edge-proxy change to normalize idempotency header (trim, remove inserted continuation markers) during translation. 3) Long-term: support canonical idempotency token in both header and payload with server-side normalized dedupe. Follow-ups: PRs created and tests added to SDK integration suite and edge translation unit tests.
follow_up_tasks: SDK: small fix to ensure header emitted atomically in streaming path (PR 4123)
Edge: add canonicalization step for X-Idempotency-Key during h2->h1 translation
Create regression test in integration lab that simulates chunked header splitting
notes_for_engineering: - Repro harness: use provided NimbleDocs snippet with adjustable chunk size; validate against local edge sidecar built from latest main.
- Consider normalizing idempotency key matching on the server: trim whitespace, collapse continuations, and optionally strip non-alphanumeric separators (configurable).
- Backport SDK fix to 1.7.x line for customers on older pinned versions.
